scenes.narration: QA Copilot turns a wall of failures into a clear decision path.

children.content: Autonomous Test Failure Triage for CQA

scenes.narration: The run lands as one hundred raw failure signals. Every one needs a decision.

children.content: Thousands of tests. Hundreds of failures.

scenes.narration: Roughly seventy resolve to automation issues. Thirty point to real product bugs. All one hundred are unresolved.
Every single one has to move through manual triage before it can be bucketed. That is the bottleneck.
Eighty percent of what engineers triage is noise.
QA Copilot is a new kind of participant in the test cycle. It runs directly on the system under test.
In the old model, every failure flows through the same path: test run, failure, manual triage.
QA Copilot intercepts the failure in real time. It steps in before the queue. Manual triage leaves the picture.
It collects evidence locally: logs, filesystem state, GPU state. Not a parser. An investigator.
The agent classifies every failure autonomously into one of four categories.
Classification is not the end. Each category drives a concrete action. This is the differentiation.
There is one principle that guides every decision the agent makes.

children.content:
A passing test that hides a product bug
is worse than a failing test.

scenes.narration: The result is a shift from a wall of raw failures to structured, root-cause-driven groups.
Failures are clustered globally across all SUTs, surfacing systemic patterns automatically.
When a product bug is confirmed, the agent assembles a structured draft instantly.
One click converts the triage result into a ready-to-file bug report.
No framework changes. Two steps to get started.
Manual triage takes hours. QA Copilot takes seconds. That is the shift.
